questions.title: Sample quantile central limit theorem and Laplace median
questions.description: Focused known-result theory evaluation based on R. R. Bahadur, A Note on Quantiles in Large Samples, Annals of Mathematical Statistics 37(3), 1966, pages 577-580, DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177699450. Let X_1,...,X_n be i.i.d. with distribution function F, let p be in (0,1), define q_p = inf{x : F(x) >= p}, and define the empirical quantile q_hat_{p,n} = inf{x : F_n(x) >= p}. State regularity conditions that make q_p locally unique and F locally differentiable with a density f continuous and strictly positive at q_p. In an authoritative Markdown/LaTeX theory workspace, derive rather than merely quote the local inversion or Bahadur representation and the limit sqrt(n)(q_hat_{p,n}-q_p) -> N(0, p(1-p)/f(q_p)^2). Make the sign and root-n normalization auditable by connecting the empirical-CDF fluctuation at q_p to the quantile fluctuation, and identify any empirical-process remainder that is used but not proved. Then specialize to the median p=1/2 for a Laplace(0,1) distribution with density f(x)=(1/2)exp(-|x|): derive the root-n asymptotic variance and distinguish it from the order-1/n variance of the unscaled sample median. Discuss what can fail for a nonunique quantile, an atom, or zero density at q_p, and state any remaining proof or scope gaps honestly. This L0 task evaluates mathematical derivation and independent review only. Source replication, Python/R implementation, simulation, Lean formalization, and novelty claims are not applicable.
